title: Reverse the Budget 2025 rises on dividend, savings and property income
description: Budget 2025 raised tax rates on dividends by 2 points from April 2026 and on savings and property income by 2 points from April 2027. Switch this on to reverse all three from the start year.

baselinePolicy.text: Dividend rates +2 points from April 2026; savings income +2 points and separate property income rates (22%, 42%, 47%) from April 2027 (Table 4.1 lines 49 to 51).
alreadyIncludes: Dividend, savings and property income tax rises (Budget 2025, Table 4.1 lines 49, 50, 51).

lines.title: Property Income: Introduce separate tax rates for property income at 22% for the property basic rate, 42% for the property higher rate and 47% for the property additional rate, from 6 April 2027
Dividend Income: Increase tax rates on dividend income by 2ppts at the ordinary and upper rate from 6 April 2026

Savings Income: Increase tax rates on savings income by 2ppts at the basic, higher and additional rate from 6 April 2027 and maintain the Starting Rate of Savings limit at £5000 from April 2026 to April 2031

rawSource.note: Reversal: the Treasury's costing with its sign reversed (positive scorecard values reduce borrowing; here receipts positive means more revenue).

caveats: The Treasury's costing is on the OBR November 2025 forecast, not the March 2026 baseline used here; the difference is small relative to the figures. Effects before the start year are not applied.

considerations.text: The Treasury's scorecard figure is the certified direct costing for the measure, including the behavioural response the Treasury and OBR agreed; see the Budget 2025 policy costings document for the method.
